---
title: "Modelling Workflow"
completion: 70
readiness: partially_implementable
---

## One Case, One Result

The model evaluates one complete user-supplied case deterministically.
Alternative designs and sensitivities are separate input records. The model
does not run an optimizer or choose a preferred case.

Input and output classes are defined on
[Inputs, Parameters and Outputs](optimisation_variables.qmd).

## Canonical Scalar Inputs

Adopted scalar inputs are stored once in `model_data/inputs.csv`, using stable,
human-readable IDs. Website pages reference those IDs, and calculation and
figure code reads the same numeric records. Explanations, evidence assessment,
scope and limitations remain on the owning website page.

The website build validates IDs, values, units, classifications, price years
and citation keys before rendering. It then calculates derived values and
currency-only conversions. Generated display variables are not model inputs
and must not be edited directly.

## Execution Order

### 1. Validate the Case Record

Check that every required user input and fixed parameter:

- has a value and unit;
- belongs to one controlled class;
- is applicable to the selected architecture;
- lies within an adopted method or product envelope; and
- does not conflict with another representation of the same quantity.

A missing required input returns **not parameterized**. A supplied value that
violates a physical or technical constraint returns **infeasible**.

### 2. Select the Architecture Branch

Select exactly one of:

- electricity export;
- centralised offshore hydrogen production; or
- decentralised turbine-integrated hydrogen production.

The architecture mapping determines which component owners are active. An
excluded component contributes neither cost nor loss.

### 3. Calculate Resource, Layout and Gross Production

The wind and layout pages return:

- the accepted turbine definition;
- turbine coordinates and farm area;
- gross and wake-adjusted production on the documented time basis; and
- layout feasibility and rejection reasons.

Where time-varying wind data are used, the owning page retains its documented
time step $\Delta t$.

### 4. Construct Physical Inventories

Calculate, before cost:

- turbine and foundation records;
- cable or pipeline route sections and physical lengths;
- platforms and equipment inventories;
- equipment counts; and
- installation-relevant masses, dimensions, lifts and loads.

Every downstream cost must consume an explicit physical quantity or a clearly
labelled top-down factor.

### 5. Size or Select Discrete Equipment

Apply the deterministic rules owned by each component page, including ceiling
or class-selection steps. The user supplies any design choice that is not
uniquely determined by the documented rules.

A failed capacity, product-class, lift, route or operating-envelope check
returns infeasible. An unresolved product set or sizing input returns not
parameterized.

### 6. Calculate Energy in Physical Order

Starting from wake-adjusted turbine production:

1. apply component efficiency or conversion equations;
2. subtract auxiliary demand at its owning subsystem;
3. apply curtailment only where a documented capacity limit requires it;
4. calculate hydrogen mass where applicable; and
5. aggregate pre-availability annual energy.

Time-varying nonlinear performance may retain the component time step.
Availability is not applied here unless the same effect is already embedded in
the energy record.

### 7. Apply Annual Availability Once

Pass pre-availability annual energy to the architecture ledger on
[Energy and Availability](energy_availability_and_annualisation.qmd).

Multiply only non-overlapping subsystem factors. A factor already embedded in
the upstream energy record is not applied again. Parallel-unit and redundancy
effects must already be combined by the component owner.

### 8. Aggregate Cost

Combine non-overlapping:

- component supply CAPEX;
- installation CAPEX;
- shared project-cost fields;
- required replacements;
- decommissioning; and
- annual OPEX.

Unknown required terms return not parameterized; they are not treated as zero.

### 9. Annualize and Report

Apply the common CRF method from
[Financial and Price-Basis Assumptions](financial_and_price_basis.qmd), then
return the endpoint and units defined on
[System Boundary and Carrier-Cost Metrics](system_boundary_and_lcoe.qmd).

## Return Status

| Status | Meaning | Cost-result behavior |
|---|---|---|
| feasible | All required inputs exist and all checks pass | Report complete applicable outputs |
| infeasible | One or more physical or technical constraints fail | Report reasons and intermediate checks; do not report a valid carrier cost |
| not_parameterized | A required value, evidence record or component method is missing | Report missing owners/inputs; do not substitute zero or report a complete carrier cost |

The returned reasons are part of the model output. A failed case must remain
auditable rather than disappearing from a set of results.
